 • GILBERT P. BAYORAN 
 Negros Occidental has recorded 5,444 dengue cases and 31 related deaths from Jan. 4 to Nov. 14 this year, representing a 3.03 percent increase compared with the same period last year.
 Data from the Provincial Epidemiology and Surveillance Unit (PESU) of the Provincial Health Office showed the province logged 160 more cases than the 5,284 recorded in 2025.
 All 31 local government units (LGUs) in the province have reported at least one suspected dengue case, according to the latest surveillance report covering Morbidity Week 45.
 La Carlota City topped the list of areas with the highest number of cases at 849, with two reported deaths.
 Silay City ranked second with 524 cases and two deaths, followed by Bago City with 513 cases and five deaths.
 Other areas in the top 10 were San Carlos City with 289 cases and no deaths; Cauayan with 278 cases and one death; Sagay City with 277 cases and one death; Cadiz City with 240 cases and seven deaths; Talisay City with 230 cases and one death; Kabankalan City with 204 cases and one death; and E.B. Magalona with 160 cases and one death.
 The surveillance data showed that dengue infections affected people across a wide age range, from as young as three months to 94 years old. 
 Children aged one to 10 years accounted for the highest number of reported cases, highlighting the vulnerability of young children to the mosquito-borne disease. | GPB
